messages:
mira: Heads-up — StellarHealth wants a pilot for the Optimize toolkit that includes: per-route quantization fallback, adaptive batching defaults, prefix/KV caching, and eval-triggered alerts. They want a tight acceptance bar before GA.

jordan: do we have a quick feasibility read? p95 latency and quality tradeoffs?

mira: their ask: p95 <= 120ms for short chat flows, and no more than 3% drop in task accuracy on our health prompt set. They also want alerts when eval concordance drops > 5pt over a 1k-window.

andrew: 120ms p95 is ambitious on hosted unless we do conservative batching (batch_size <= 4) + per-tenant prefix cache hits. For Dedicated it's fine with burst slots. Quant fallback per-route is doable: run quantized model by default, fallback to FP16 on quality regression.

sasha: +1. Need to define the rollback surface: do we have an automatic fallback policy w/ thresholds? e.g. if eval score delta > 3% for 1k requests then flip route to high-precision variant.

mira: propose launch scope (pilot): 1) adaptive batching defaults (desktop/mobile presets), 2) KV/prefix caching for repeated sessions, 3) per-route quantization with manual canary + eval-triggered auto-fallback, 4) alerting webhook to customer (and to ops). Not including automatic online recompile or new kernel selection for pilot.

jordan: suggest we pin model variants for pilot to avoid noisy kernel changes. Also provide a char-to-token mapping doc so SH can estimate token costs.

andrew: acceptance criteria draft: 
- perf: p95 <= 120ms on 90% of pilot routes (measured over 24h windows)
- quality: task accuracy drop <= 3% vs FP16 baseline on the team's eval set
- alerting: eval-triggered webhook delivered within 5m of window close when concordance delta > 5pt
- observability: token-level cost per-route visible in console

sasha: operational constraints: we need a per-customer cache quota and eviction policy. default: 5GB KV cache per tenant, LRU. If they want more, sales + infra review.

mira: customer asked for a control plane knob to opt out of quant fallback for specific routes. We should expose a route flag: `quant_fallback: on|off|auto`.

jordan: quick config sketch (pilot):
```yaml
route: /stella/chat
quant_profile: r4-24q
quant_fallback: auto  # auto = try quant, fallback to fp16 on eval regression
batching: preset: mobile_small
cache: prefix: enabled, size_mb: 512
eval_alerts: threshold_pts: 5, window: 1000, webhook: https://hooks.stellar/alerts
```

andrew: timeline proposal: 2-week sprint to implement flags + basic alerting and demo to StellarHealth. 1-week pilot run with telemetry gating. Rolling to GA after pilot + postmortem.

sasha: risks: 1) noisy eval signal causing flapping — need hysteresis (e.g., require 2 windows before auto-fallback), 2) cache warm-up makes early latency look bad, 3) token-cost surprises for customer.

mira: mitigation ideas: add hysteresis (2 windows), show expected warm-up curve in onboarding doc, and include cost simulation tool in console for pilot routes.

andrew: action items: @jordan to draft SDK/route flag spec, @sasha to write cache quota + eviction proposal, @mira to draft pilot acceptance sheet and customer-facing runbook.

jordan: I’ll push a minimal PR for the route flags and a small e2e test (simulate degredation -> fallback). ETA EOD Friday.

sasha: I’ll post the cache proposal in #eng-infra by tomorrow and tag infra leads.

mira: ops-bot: create pilot-tracker with tags `optimize-pilot` and `stellarhealth`

ops-bot: Created ticket TID-3421: "optimize-pilot/stellahealth" — assignees: mira, jordan, sasha, andrew.

mira: perfect. Keeping scope tight: no kernel-level perf work for pilot. If pilot signals we need compile changes, prioritize in next cycle.

jordan: noted. Also adding a small eval harness that runs the customer's 500 prompt subset every 10m and publishes a simple concordance metric to the alerting pipeline.

andrew: once pilot acceptance criteria are green we should capture a short runbook for GA: expected defaults, knobs, SLOs, and rollback steps.

mira: thanks all. Sync tomorrow 10am to review PRs and pilot tracker. :thumbsup:
